paper.title: Tracking Most Significant Shifts in Infinite-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Non-stationary infinite-armed bandits with beta-regular reservoir
unmapped: Initial mean rewards of newly sampled arms drawn i.i.d. from a beta-regular reservoir: kappa_1 x^beta <= P(mu_0(a) > 1-x) <= kappa_2 x^beta
Rested non-stationarity: an adaptive adversary changes the mean of an arm only after it is played
Regret measured against the maximal reward value 1: R_T = sum_t (1 - mu_t(a_t))
The learner knows the reservoir exponent beta (used in the subsampling rate)
Non-stationarity measured by realized (agent-dependent) counts/variations L, V, L_R, V_R and significant shifts
settings.definition_quote: When the agent samples arm $a_t \in \mc{A}$ at round $t$, it observes a random reward $Y_t(a_t) \in [0,1]$ with mean $\mu_t(a_t) \in [0,1]$ whose value is randomly drawn from a {\em mean reservoir distribution}. The reward of this chosen arm in the subsequent round is then decided according to an adaptive adversary with access to prior decisions

unmapped: Means mu_t(a) may vary over time but stay within alpha of a fixed reference profile mu(a) (alpha-mild corruption, per-round deviation bound rather than a total budget)
settings.definition_quote: We say a finite-armed non-stationary bandit environment $\{ \mu_t(a)\}$ over horizon $T$ with armset $\mc{A}_0$ is {\bf $\alpha$-mildly corrupt} for $\alpha>0$ if there exists a {\bf reference} reward profile $\{ \mu(a)\}$ such that $\forall t \in [T] , a \in \mc{A}_0: |\mu_t(a) - \mu(a) | \leq \alpha$.

symbols.beta_res: shape parameter of the beta-regular reservoir distribution
symbols.L_chg: realized count of changes in played arms' means
symbols.V_var: realized total variation of played arms' means

conditions: Assumption 1: beta-regular reservoir with constants kappa_1, kappa_2
Base algorithm satisfies Assumption 2 (gap-dependent regret under alpha-mild corruption)

source.label: thm:blackbox
source.quote: Under \Cref{ass:reservoir} with $\beta \geq 1$, \Cref{alg:blackbox} with $S_m := \ceil{ 2^{m \cdot \frac{\beta}{\beta+1}} }$ satisfies, w.p. $1-O(1/T)$: ${\bf R}_T \leq \tilde{O} \left( (L+1)^{\frac{1}{\beta+1}}  T^{\frac{\beta}{\beta+1}} \land (V^{\frac{1}{\beta+2}} T^{\frac{\beta+1}{\beta+2}} + T^{\frac{\beta}{\beta+1}}) \right).

results.notes: Probability 1-O(1/T). Regret is sum of 1-mu_t(a_t), i.e. against the per-round max value 1. L and V are realized agent-dependent quantities, not known to the learner (parameter-free).

symbols.L_chg: realized count of changes in played arms' means
symbols.V_var: realized total variation of played arms' means

source.label: thm:blackbox
source.quote: If $\beta < 1$, \Cref{alg:blackbox} with $S_m := \ceil{  2^{m \cdot \beta/2}  }$ satisfies w.p. $1 - O(1/T)$: ${\bf R}_T \leq \tilde{O} \left( \sqrt{(L+1) \cdot T} \land ( V^{1/3} T^{2/3} + \sqrt{T} ) \right).

results.notes: Suboptimal for beta<1 per the paper; proof only sketched.

symbols.beta_res: shape parameter of the beta-regular reservoir distribution
symbols.V_R: realized total rotting variation of played arms' means

conditions: beta-regular reservoir (only the lower bound kappa_1 x^beta on tail mass is needed per the paper's discussion)

source.label: cor:elim-bounds
source.quote: \Cref{alg:elim} satisfies, w.p. at least $1-1/T$: ${\bf R}_T \leq \tilde{O}\left( (\Lsig + 1)^{\frac{1}{\beta+1}}  T^{\frac{\beta}{\beta+1}} \land ( V_R^{\frac{1}{\beta+2}}  T^{\frac{\beta+1}{\beta+2}} + T^{\frac{\beta}{\beta+1}} ) \right).

results.notes: Holds for all beta>0, parameter-free in L_sig and V_R. Paper notes L_sig <= L_R. Derived from Theorem 4 (regret = O~(sum over episodes of length^(beta/(beta+1)))), which is not recorded separately since it is in terms of random episode lengths.

symbols.alpha_c: mild corruption level: max deviation of mu_t(a) from reference mu(a)
symbols.C_0: constant free of t, T and the arm set

conditions: gaps Delta_i defined w.r.t. reference profile; sum only over arms with Delta_i >= 4*alpha_c
results.notes: Bound taken from Assumption 2: holds w.p. >= 1-1/T for all t <= T with t in place of T in the 6 t alpha term; recorded with T. Regret is against the best fixed arm in the subsample, measured via means.
